title: Role Model Debates Maine Fame on Chicken Shop Date
summary:
As far as current pop music goes, Role Model is probably Maine's most famous export. But what about celebrities in general? While guesting on the Friday (Oct. 2) premiere episode of Amelia Dimoldenberg's final season of "Chicken Shop Date," the singer born Tucker Pillsbury pondered whether he has the most star power of everyone from his home state.

"Anna Kendrick's from Maine," he pointed out, while the show's host noted that famed horror author Stephen King is also from the Pine Tree State.

"He's probably sold more stuff than me," Pillsbury said of King, who indeed is one of the best-selling novelists of all time. "Got more money."

After a bit of back-and-forth, Dimoldenberg told the singer: "You're not as successful as Stephen King, no. That's just a fact."

"You're starting to hurt my feelings," Pillsbury replied. "[He has a] whole different job."

The jury is still out on who exactly is Maine's most famous celebrity, but other front-runners include actor Patrick Dempsey and sports personality Erin Andrews. And while Role Model may not quite have the sales numbers that King has, the musician recently scored his very first top 10 album on the Billboard 200 with "Chuck Timely & The Hourglass," which amassed 24,000 copies sold in the United States in its first week out, according to Luminate.
why_it_matters: It is a light example of how artists talk about fame, and chart numbers like first-week sales show how success is measured in music.
